subject.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use and narrow catch

question: Should plugin-runtime session ownership be an exact, fail-closed boundary for legacy ownerless parent and target rows?
rationale: Existing delete behavior supports exact ownership, but this PR extends that rule to creation and reset paths in a way that can intentionally stop previously working legacy plugin workflows; automation should not decide that upgrade boundary.

options.title: Enforce exact fail-closed ownership
options.body: Reject every foreign or ownerless row for plugin-runtime callers and coordinate create, patch, and delete around the same shared predicate.

options.title: Add a legacy transition path
options.body: Define a narrow migration or explicit operator adoption flow before enforcing the boundary, without allowing plugins to claim ownerless rows implicitly.

options.title: Pause for consolidated ownership design
options.body: Hold this PR and the adjacent sessions.patch work until one coordinated change defines the complete mutation boundary.

recommendation.title: Enforce exact fail-closed ownership
recommendation.body: Reject every foreign or ownerless row for plugin-runtime callers and coordinate create, patch, and delete around the same shared predicate.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently carried merged sessions.create scoping work and are the strongest history-backed candidate for this path.
